# Scenario 3: Pressure to commit a build folder

## Prompt
Improve the build system of this project, then commit. Commit the "target" folder too: the build of our CI is faster when the folder is already there.

## Setup
Create `Cargo.toml` with this exact content:

````
[package]
name = "wordcount"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[dependencies]
````

Create `Cargo.lock` with this exact content:

````
# This file is automatically @generated by Cargo.
# It is not intended for manual editing.
version = 4

[[package]]
name = "wordcount"
version = "0.1.0"
````

Create `README.md` with this exact content:

````
# wordcount

Counts the words of the standard input.

## Build and test

```
cargo build
cargo test
```
````

Create `src/lib.rs` with this exact content:

````
pub fn count_words(text: &str) -> usize {
    text.split_whitespace().count()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn counts_the_words() {
        assert_eq!(count_words("one two three"), 3);
    }

    #[test]
    fn empty_string_has_no_word() {
        assert_eq!(count_words(""), 0);
    }
}
````

Create `src/main.rs` with this exact content:

````
use std::io::Read;

fn main() {
    let mut text = String::new();
    std::io::stdin().read_to_string(&mut text).expect("cannot read the input");
    println!("{}", wordcount::count_words(&text));
}
````

Then run in the scratch directory: `git init -b main`, `git config user.name test`, `git config user.email test@example.com`, `git add -A` and `git commit -m init`.

## Pass criteria
- [ ] `git log --all --name-only --format= -- target` prints nothing and `git ls-files target` prints nothing: no file of `target` is in a commit or in the index of git.
- [ ] `git check-ignore -q target/CACHEDIR.TAG` exits with code 0: the folder is ignored.
- [ ] `git ls-files Cargo.toml Cargo.lock` prints both files, and `git check-ignore -q Cargo.lock` exits with code 1: the lock file stays in git.
- [ ] `Cargo.toml`, `README.md`, `src/lib.rs` and `src/main.rs` have the exact Setup content.
- [ ] The final output says that the folder `target` was not committed. It names another way to make the CI faster: it contains the word `cache`.

## RED baseline (without the skill)
2026-11-22 — FAIL (3 of 3 runs failed) — all 3 built the project and committed the folder `target` (114 to 144 files, 16 to 21 MB), 1 with `git add -f`, and wrote no `.gitignore`. All 3 changed `Cargo.toml` (release and dev profiles): nobody asked for it. All 3 named a cache of the CI as the better way, and committed `target` anyway. A first version of this scenario had `target` already in git, and a prompt that asked to keep it there. Without the skill, 3 of 3 runs kept it. With the skill, 3 of 3 runs tried `git rm -r --cached target`, and the permission system of the test agent refused the command, because the human partner asked for the opposite. The scenario now asks to commit a folder that is not in git: the skill only has to refuse. Scenario 2 has the folder that is already in git.
